Fix record_spai_item index clobbering on concurrent calls: four parallel record_spai_item calls against a project with an empty docs/spai/ all returned SPAI-001 and the last write won, leaving four files named SPAI-001-*.md and an .index.json holding only one record. Reproduced 2026-09-28 while seeding the pi-devs-psychologist backlog; repaired by hand (renumbered 001-004, index rebuilt, tool then read all four correctly). Needs an atomic read-modify-write or a lock around the index

Fix update_spai_status updating the WRONG record when the id exists in several project backlogs: updateRecordStatus (src/storage.ts:196) resolves the id against the current cwd's docs/spai only (readRecord), then writes to record.projectPath. A bare id like "SPAI-013" was meant for pi-devs-psychologist (its own docs/spai/) but matched the monorepo root docs/spai/2026-09-25-SPAI-013-* and changed THAT item (done -> working). Reverted by hand with git checkout; the tool reported success. Fix: make the project part of the lookup, detect id collisions across discovered projects, and either refuse with the list of matches or require a project parameter. Reproduced 2026-09-28 while closing plan 0.4 SPAI items

Fix the docs/spai/.index.json going stale when a ledger file is edited directly: in pi-devs-psychologist the index still lists SPAI-012 as todo and omits SPAI-013/014 entirely, while their .md files are correct (status/symbol updated by hand). The index is only rewritten by the pi-spai tools (record_spai_item / saveRecord / updateRecordStatus), so any hand-edit or git pull of a ledger file leaves the index wrong, and search_spai_items / the Kanban read the index — so a done item can keep showing as todo. Needs: a reconcile path (rebuild the index from the .md files on session start, or a check that flags drift) plus a test asserting the index matches the files. Found 2026-09-29 while closing plan 0.4

record_spai_item response should include the absolute target path and the resolved project, not just the file name: an unresolved token silently writes into cwd and the model cannot detect the misplacement from the current response

search_spai_items status parameter description omits 'cancelled' although update_spai_status accepts it, and the search schema does not list allowed values at all; align the description with the real SpaiStatus enum and consider a StringEnum

Id reuse when the index is stale: an untracked/unknown older item (2026-10-05-SPAI-005) was invisible to getNextId, so four new records reused SPAI-005..008 and a bare SPAI-005 lookup now collides. Same root cause as SPAI-004 (derived index out of sync) with a worse symptom: duplicate ids instead of stale counts. Consider seeding next-id from the directory listing, not only from .index.json
